title: Race to the bottom

definition.text: A situation in which governments, firms or individuals compete by steadily lowering standards or regulations to cut costs and attract economic activity.

facts.text: Unlike ordinary competition, which tends to improve goods and services, it erodes labour laws, tax rates and environmental rules.
Places with stricter labour or environmental rules or higher taxes can lose business to less regulated places, pushing them to lower their own standards.
The term traces to US Justice Louis Brandeis, describing states competing to attract corporations in the late 1800s and early 1900s.
Firms may move to countries that do not require them to treat chemical waste before dumping it, avoiding costly treatment.
Globalisation lets a producer unconcerned with biodiversity undercut one who cares, driving a race to the bottom in conservation rules.
Whether it really happens is debated: Daniel Drezner calls it a myth, and a 2022 study found no evidence of it in labour standards, though Nita Rudra found it in developing countries.
Some US states pursue the opposite, a 'race to the top', with innovative environmental policies other states may copy.

contested_note: Scholars disagree on whether a race to the bottom actually occurs, with empirical evidence on both sides.

title: Rio Conventions

definition.text: The three conventions agreed at the June 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro: on climate change (UNFCCC), biological diversity (CBD) and desertification (UNCCD).

facts.text: The summit also produced Agenda 21, the Forest Principles and the Rio Declaration.
The CBD's three objectives are conserving biodiversity, using its components sustainably and sharing fairly the benefits of genetic resources.
The UNFCCC aims to stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations at a level that prevents dangerous human interference with the climate system.
The UNCCD links sustainable land management to land degradation and aims at land degradation neutrality, with a focus on restoring drylands.

related: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification

title: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
article: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development

definition.text: A short document of 27 principles, produced at the 1992 Earth Summit, to guide countries in future sustainable development.

facts.text: Its first principle says sustainable development is chiefly about people, who are entitled to healthy, productive lives in harmony with nature.
Principle 15 states the precautionary principle, to be applied by states according to their capabilities.
Principle 16 encourages the polluter pays principle where it serves the public interest and does not distort trade and investment.
Principle 10 stresses citizens' participation and access to environmental information, later elaborated by the Aarhus Convention.
It built on the 1972 Stockholm Declaration, aiming to set out principles states can write into their own laws.
It raised environmental awareness, but evidence from 2007 suggested little of its environmental goals had been achieved.

definition.text: Managing space and resources by making and carrying out plans that limit how land and space can be used and developed.

facts.text: It is usually done by national, regional or local governments and balances competing demands on land from the state, the market and local communities.
It is needed because the economy, housing and environmental protection all compete for space.
Its disciplines include land-use, urban, regional, transport and environmental planning, as well as maritime spatial planning.

definition.text: An ethical practice of responsibly planning and managing resources, which can be applied to the environment, economics, property and more.

facts.text: The word comes from the duties of a household steward, a keeper of the hall.
Natural resource management focuses on how management affects quality of life for present and future generations, which is called stewardship.
Stewardship councils certify products, such as the Forest Stewardship Council since 1993 and the Marine Stewardship Council since 1996.
